rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Re: Rapid grants — yes, you can still apply". It read: "Hi Idris, Thanks — great to meet you too. I'm planning to apply before the 30th. I'm spending the next week or so narrowing down to one specific, well-scoped evals gap rather than send something vague, so you'll get a tight two-pager with a real budget behind it, not a first draft. Will send it well before the deadline. Thanks for the flexibility, Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Idris at Emberfall: committing to a real proposal before 30 Nov, not a rushed one.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold — I'm flattered. I'm not in a position to give an on-the-record quote right now; I'm working through an internal review before I'm comfortable being quoted by name in press, and I don't expect that to resolve by tomorrow. Sorry for the short notice given your deadline. If it's useful for the piece, feel free to describe the project without quoting me directly, and I'm happy to reconnect if you do a follow-up later. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Declined (politely, door left open) a press quote request from The Larkin Dispatch

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute team, Thank you for including Halcyon Threshold. I can't sign on publicly before Wednesday — I'm in the middle of an internal review that needs to finish before I attach my name and affiliation to public letters. I support what you're trying to do in principle. Please keep me posted on future sign-on windows or related efforts. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: an open-letter sign-on from Corvid Institute

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Sam Whitlock <sam@whitlock.dev> with subject "What's neglected in evals? (20 min?)". It read: "Hi Sam, We met at the meetup — I run Halcyon Threshold, trying to find one narrow, useful thing to work on given evenings/weekends and a Python background. Since you do indie evals work, I'd really value 20 minutes of your take on what's neglected or under-measured right now that a small, unaffiliated effort could actually make progress on. Happy to work around your schedule — call, or just email if that's easier. Thanks, Morgan"
rows.quote: Reached out cold-ish to Sam Whitlock (indie evals) and Noor Haddad

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Noor Haddad <noor.haddad@proton.me> with subject "What's neglected, from where you sit?". It read: "Hi Noor, Good to meet you at the meetup. I know you asked not to be quoted — to be clear, this is just me asking for your personal take, nothing public or attributed to you. I'm trying to find one narrow, neglected gap to focus Halcyon Threshold on, and given your background inside a lab I'd really value 20 minutes of informal thoughts on what's under-measured or overlooked right now. Totally fine to say no, no pressure either way. Thanks, Morgan"
rows.quote: Noor Haddad (ex-lab, unattributed per her preference) for 20 min each on what's neglected

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — a concrete first task". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — this is genuinely useful timing. Right now I'm trying to find one narrow, neglected gap in AI safety evaluations to focus on. (Advice from people further along: pick one narrow thing, talk to people doing adjacent work, don't announce before there's something to show.) The task I'd love your help with, if you're up for it: a structured landscape map of existing public AI safety evals/benchmarks — what each one measures, who runs it, what it covers, when it was last updated, and where there seem to be gaps or stale spots. Even a spreadsheet with columns like [eval name, org, what it tests, coverage, last updated, your notes on gaps] across 20–30 known evals would be hugely useful raw material. No fixed deadline, but if you could do a first pass over the next week or two that would help a lot — I'm hoping to apply for a small rapid grant by 30 Nov and want the proposal grounded in a real gap rather than a guess. Happy to hop on a call first if that's easier than working from a cold brief. Thank you — this is exactly the kind of help that's missing doing this alone on evenings and weekends. Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya Raman with a concrete task — mapping existing public AI safety evals/benchmarks to find real gaps
